children.text: In the hills of Oslob in southern Cebu, countless threads of water pour like a curtain over an entire mossy limestone wall. It is only about
10 minutes
by habal-habal from the whale shark watching area, so it is a favorite place to cool off in the turquoise pool after the encounter.
Tumalog Falls is tucked into the hillside of Luka and Tumalog villages in Oslob, at the southeastern tip of Cebu, about
3km

from Tan-awan, the whale shark watching area. Unlike an ordinary falls that drops in a single stream, hundreds of fine threads of water rain down across an entire high limestone wall, earning it nicknames like "curtain falls" and "rain curtain." Locals also call it Mag-ambak Falls, and it ranks alongside the whale sharks as one of Oslob's signature sights.

Over long years, lime-rich water flowing down the wall has left layered deposits that form step-like folds, and moss and ferns have grown over them, creating a distinctive mix of green rock and white streams. The pool below is a milky turquoise and mostly waist- to chest-deep, so even weak swimmers can wade in comfortably. Published heights vary wildly, from around
to nearly
, so it is more accurate to think of it simply as a wall tall enough that you have to tip your head all the way back to see the top.
The flow depends heavily on rain. In
March 2024

the falls dried up so badly that the water no longer reached the ground, and the Oslob local government temporarily closed it. Besides the El Niño drought, sinkholes in the mountain that likely formed after Typhoon Odette in
December 2021
were blamed for diverting the water. The falls stayed dry for a while even into the rainy season until the water returned and it reopened on
October 30, 2024
, and visitor accounts through 2026 show it flowing and open. The water also serves as a backup supply for 13 of Oslob's 21 barangays, so it is a place the community treasures.
Most travelers stop here after seeing the whale sharks at dawn in
Oslob
, partly to rinse off the seawater, then continue to
Sumilon Island

or Oslob Church in the afternoon. An hour or two at the falls is enough and the walking is short, so it suits families with children, couples who love photography and anyone covering southern Cebu in a day. Keep in mind, though, that the flow can thin out late in the dry season, so your impression of the falls can vary greatly depending on when you go.

The fine streams coming down the wall do not pound down but scatter like a shower. Stand beneath them and cool droplets drum on your shoulders like a natural shower, which is also perfect for washing off the seawater after the whale shark encounter.

The pool in front of the falls is wide and mostly waist- to chest-deep. The cold water is great for cooling down on a hot day, and if you are not a confident swimmer you can rent a life vest on site for about
The falls roughly face east, so around
, when the sun shines from behind the streams, light beams and small rainbows appear in the spray. It is also before the tour groups arrive and the pool is quiet, making it the best time for photos.

blocks.title: Ride a habal-habal down the steep road

children.text: Cars cannot go down the steep road from the roadside parking area to the falls, so you ride a habal-habal motorcycle taxi. Hanging on behind the driver down the forest road is a short little adventure that makes the falls memorable.

blocks.title: Stroll the lower stream and small pools

children.text: Water from the main pool spills over a low stepped weir and runs between the rocks, forming several more jade-green pools below. The lower area, with its bamboo groves and thatched huts, is quieter than the main pool and good for dipping your feet and resting.

blocks.title: Rock hollow left of the pool

children.text: Guides mention a small rock hollow at the base of the wall on the left as you face the falls, running down to the water's edge. It is not a deep cave, but you can see up close how the limestone wall has been carved, so it is worth a quick look after checking that the floor is not slippery.

blocks.title: A full Oslob day with the whale sharks

children.text: Snorkeling with whale sharks at dawn, Tumalog Falls in the morning, then the Sumilon Island sandbar or Oslob Church in the afternoon is the classic flow for a southern Cebu trip. Most joined tours from Cebu City follow this order too.

Tour groups that have finished whale shark watching start flooding the falls around
, so the key is to arrive before then. If you stay an extra day in Oslob, you can also split it into a whale shark day and a falls day and arrive at the falls right at opening time.

items.subtitle: Private car with driver or joined tour

children.text: Leave your lodging in Cebu City or Mactan and drive down the southern coastal road
Arrive in Tan-awan, register and snorkel with the whale sharks
Swim and relax at Tumalog Falls
Lunch of grilled fish or kinilaw at a seaside eatery in Oslob

Arrive in Cebu City or Mactan
Oslob is about
3.5–4.5 hours

one way from Cebu City, so you spend most of the day in the car. The southern road gets more congested as the afternoon goes on, so limit stops on the way back to one, and if you are short on energy we recommend staying a night in Oslob.
Philippine Airlines, Cebu Pacific and Philippines AirAsia fly direct from Manila to Mactan-Cebu International Airport (CEB) in about
1 hour 30 minutes
. From the airport to Oslob is about
3.5–4.5 hours
by car, so if you land late in the afternoon it is easier to stay a night in Cebu City or Mactan and leave at dawn the next day to make the whale shark watching hours.
From the Cebu South Bus Terminal, take a Ceres bus marked "Bato via Oslob" or bound for Santander. Buses run roughly every hour, with early-morning first departures.
The trip takes about
3.5–4.5 hours
, and fares are about
depending on ordinary or air-conditioned service; figures differ between sources, so check at the terminal.
Ask the conductor to let you off at the Tumalog Falls junction in Luka. From the junction to the falls entrance, take one of the waiting habal-habal.
From the Tan-awan whale shark area it is about
10 minutes
by habal-habal for about
one way, and from Oslob town about
15–20 minutes
for about
one way. Agree on a round-trip price and ask the driver to wait, and you will not need to find a ride back.
From the roadside parking area to the falls is a steep concrete road that cars cannot go down. A habal-habal for just this stretch costs about
per person round trip; you can walk down, but the climb back is long and steep, so it is not recommended in the midday heat.
From Cebu City or Mactan, drive about
along the southern coastal road through Carcar, Argao and Boljoon. A same-day round-trip charter to Oslob costs about
for a sedan and about

for a van, usually including the driver and fuel. Split among 4 to 6 people it costs more than the bus, but it saves a lot of time and lets you stop wherever you like. Cars park at the upper parking area, and you go down to the falls by habal-habal or on foot.
If you are staying in Dumaguete on Negros, take the ferry from Sibulan port to Liloan port in Santander. The crossing takes about
20–30 minutes
and costs about
including surcharges. From Liloan port, the falls are about
20–30 minutes
north by bus or habal-habal, which is actually closer than coming down from Cebu City.
Joined tours with pre-dawn pickup from lodgings in Cebu City or Mactan, bundling the whale shark watching fee, Tumalog Falls or Sumilon Island, and lunch, cost about
per person. Some packages make you choose between the falls and Sumilon or charge the falls entrance and habal-habal fares separately, so check the inclusions in the booking agency's latest notice.
At Tumalog Falls, everything comes down to how much water is flowing, so timing matters. In
November–February

, as the rainy season winds down, the mountain holds plenty of water so the curtain covers the whole wall, and with less rain the pool tends to stay clear. This is when flow and weather are best balanced.
Late in the dry season, in
March–May

, the weather is clear and the water vivid, but the streams thin noticeably, and in the severe drought of 2024 the falls dried up completely and closed. If you go in this period, check with the Oslob tourism office, your lodging or tour operator the day before. In the
June–October

rainy season the flow is abundant and impressive, but after heavy rain the water turns muddy and the steep road becomes slippery. On days when a typhoon passes, the southern road and ferries can stop running.

The best time of day is early morning right after opening. Whale shark watching runs year-round, only in the early morning, and both the watching area and the falls get crowded in peak season, on weekends, during Holy Week and over the year-end holidays, so we recommend going on a weekday.

To stay near the falls, the Tan-awan coast with the whale shark watching area is the most convenient. Small resorts and guesthouses within walking distance of the watching area are clustered here, and the falls are only about
10 minutes
away by habal-habal. Guesthouses on the Oslob mainland coast cost about
a night, and if you prefer a quiet atmosphere, Oslob town with its church and heritage park is also good. For a special night, there is Bluewater Sumilon Island Resort on Sumilon Island at about
a night.

At the falls entrance there is only a small shop selling water, snacks and drinks, plus changing rooms and toilets; there is no proper restaurant. Meals are usually eaten at simple eateries in Tan-awan and along the Oslob coastal road, where freshly caught grilled fish, kinilaw (raw fish cured in vinegar) and chicken barbecue are popular. On the way back to Cebu City, Carcar's lechon and chicharon and Argao's torta (a sponge cake made with tuba palm wine) are also well-known treats.
Opening hours are roughly
but are not strictly enforced. Arrive before
for fewer people and better light.
Entrance and habal-habal fares are cash only. There is no ATM on site, so bring plenty of small bills of
or less and coins.
Settle both the round trip and waiting time with your habal-habal driver before setting off. Most people who plan to ride down and walk back up change their minds at the foot of the steep climb.
The pool floor and rocks are slippery, so wear water shoes or sports sandals with grippy soles.
Spray carries a long way, and near the falls your camera lens gets wet quickly. Keep your phone in a waterproof pouch and bring a cloth to wipe the lens.
There are changing rooms and toilets at the entrance, so wear your swimsuit underneath and pack dry clothes and a towel in a plastic bag.

When booking a tour from Cebu, be sure to check whether Tumalog Falls is included or whether you must choose between it and Sumilon Island. If you really want to see the falls, pick a package that includes them by default.
Late in the dry season, in
March–May
, check the Oslob tourism office's notices or ask your lodging about the water flow before fixing your plans.
Tumalog Falls can close without notice when the flow drops or heavy rain pours. From
March to October 2024
it dried up and was closed for more than
7 months
, so check the latest notices before you visit.
The road down from the parking area to the falls is very steep. Hold on tight on the habal-habal, and after rain ask the driver to go slowly.
Walking up and down means a steep climb with little shade. If you have weak knees, are older or have small children with you, use a habal-habal.
The rocks under the streams are very slippery with moss. Do not climb the wall or jump from high rocks, and stay out of any area the staff close off.
Right after heavy rain the water can turn muddy and the current can get stronger. If heavy rain starts upstream, get out of the water at once.
There are reports that the entrance fee has ranged from free to
depending on who manages it. Get a ticket or receipt, and if you are asked for more than the official rate, ask for the tourism office rate.
The falls' water is a backup supply for the villages. Do not use soap or shampoo, and always take your trash with you.
In Tan-awan, about
10 minutes
away by habal-habal, you can swim with whale sharks almost every day. The town has a coral-stone church and the ruins of a Spanish-era cuartel.
About
15–20 minutes
by car to Bancogon pier and another
15 minutes
or so by boat brings you to the Philippines' first marine protected area and its shape-shifting white sandbar.
About
1.5–2 hours
by car to Badian on the island's west coast, these falls are famous for canyoneering down a turquoise gorge by jumping into its pools.
In Sibonga on the way back to Cebu City, about
2 hours
away by car. Pilgrims gather at this castle-like church for its devotion to the miraculous Virgin Mary.
A university city on Negros, about
20–30 minutes
by ferry from Liloan port, and the gateway to Apo Island and Siquijor.
